names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Ηλίας, Πρόβος και Άρης», with the rank word left off. The page's text gives an alternative in passing, «Πρόβος (ή Πρόμος)», which is recorded in the attestation and not stored as a second form.

The calendar’s own name page for him is «Пров Египтянин, мч.»; the grade is stripped and the epithet kept, the day line itself declining the bare forename and putting «египтян» after all three. `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

feast.note: The same menologion day this folder’s other rows already carry, so there is no second day and none is noted. THE LINE GIVES HIM A YEAR THIS FOLDER DID NOT HAVE: it closes «(308)» over all three names, and his companion `ares-19-december` already carries 308 from saint.gr’s name-block for that man alone. The two readings agree, so the year is written into `dates` here. THE CALENDAR ALSO CALLS THE THREE «египтян», Egyptians, which no other source in this folder does. HE IS NOT `probus-16-december`, `probus-9-july` or `probus-of-tarsus`, who stand on other menologion days and are stored otherwise. The reading this calendar links, `/Life/life3147.htm`, stands behind all three men at once and was NOT opened; this folder’s life is already written out of its other source. Nothing on the day page is under his name.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Ηλίας, Πρόβος και Άρης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. **The entry enumerates its company — three named men — so it is a folder each, and each relates the other two.** The page's whole narrative is two sentences: the holy Elias, Probus — or Promus, as it gives him a second name — and Ares came of Egypt, and inspired by their warm faith went about to various cities and served the persecuted Christians; at Ascalon they were arrested, held to their confession of Jesus Christ, and were condemned to death by the judge Firmilianus; Elias and Probus were beheaded and Ares gave up his holy soul in the flames. **Only Ares carries a year, and only in the page's name-block head, «Αγιος Αρης (; - 308)»; Elias and Probus carry none at all, and none is inferred for them from his.** It names Egypt and Ascalon and no coordinate is proposed. It prints no hymn. **An identity question named and not decided: saint.gr keeps an «Όσιος Άρης» on 13 Δεκεμβρίου too, one of the ascetics of the Egyptian desert whose sayings are in the Evergetinos, drafted in that day's batch as `ares-of-the-egyptian-desert`. Two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, and these two Ares are a desert elder who died in peace and a martyr burnt at Ascalon under Firmilianus; nothing is merged.**
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (2 October 2026).

death.note: The first year this folder has carried. The Russian line closes «(308)» over the three Egyptians together, and the same year stands already on the folder of the third of them, `ares-19-december`, out of saint.gr’s own name-block head for that man. Two books, one year, and no year of birth from either.
